There was once a mysterious island called Isola,\n
home to a tribe of lost refugees.\n
Many generations had flourished on the island, but the tribal chief was now troubled.\n
Life had begun to slowly diminish. Where have the birds gone?\n
The fish? Is Isola dying? An expedition is to be formed,\n
and the chief prays for guidance from above...\n
With divine guidance, the expedition was planned and launched.\n
After days of wandering aimlessly through the jungle, they realized that they were lost.\n
As their hope was failing, they crashed through some thorny brambles \n
and stumbled onto something they could not have expected.\n
They found themselves at the edge of a clearing on the eastern shore of the island.\n
Rooted in the sandy silt of a dry creek bed, an enormous, dying tree stood forsaken.\n
Do you need help getting started?\n
beautiful runes are visible on the rocks.\n
Before anything lived on Isola, there was only a single sapling.\n
How it came to be on the island no one can possibly know.\n
The tree grew and thrived. Over hundreds of years it became strong and ancient.\n
It was so full of life, and so deeply rooted, that the island itself\n
was infused with a unique and potent life force.\n
The power of nature and the power of magic alike \n
emanated from the essence of this great tree. This is what enabled\n
the inhabitants of Isola to perform such wonders as they did.\n
But what has become of the tree? \n
Is it being undone by some great illness or curse?\n
If it dies, that which makes Isola special will be lost forever...\n
Once a lone sapling on a barren island...\n
Now, once more a thriving and mighty banyan tree, healed and showing new growth.\n
Life and balance, nature and magic, have been restored to Isola.\n
As your villagers continue to grow and thrive, they are drawn to the mysterious tree.\n
The importance of the Tree of Life, will never again be forgotten...\n

Let's explore the area...
 click and hold the mouse button 
 anywhere on the ground and drag the 
 mouse to move around the village.

Good! This is how you move about 
 the island. Feel free to explore your
 little village.
Let's get to know one of the villagers...\n find and click a villager to select them.\n

Perfect! A white circle shows which 
 villager is selected. See important 
 details about this villager, like their 
 name, at the bottom of the screen.

Let's move a villager...
 click and hold the mouse button 
 on a villager and drag the mouse
 to move them.

Excellent! Moving villagers influences their 
 behavior. Drag and drop villagers anywhere 
 you like to help them explore useful or 
 interesting places in the village.

Your little villagers must be hungry,
 after their long expedition. Fortunately, 
 there are some blackberries available. 
 Just drag someone to the blackberry bush
 and they will attempt to gather some berries.

Great job! Your villagers can survive on 
 these blackberries until they find a more 
 sustainable source of food.

Your villagers would benefit from a 
 warm and cozy fire. First, drag an 
 adult villager to this pile of 
 driftwood, so they can gather wood.
Well done. There is a pile of dry firewood in\n the fire pit.\n
Kindling is also needed to start a fire.\n Drag your villager to this patch of dry grass.\n
Good. Your villager put an armful of dry grass into the fire pit.\n

With dry firewood and kindling, all that's
 necessary to start the fire is to
 drag a villager to the fire pit.

Well done! Your tribe can now enjoy
 the benefits of a hot, crackling
 fire on those chilly nights.

Your villagers interact with many
 locations around the map. Let's
 start by dragging one of them to this
 hut that needs some repair.

Excellent! This hut is the love shack and is
 needed for villagers to 'discuss' having a baby. Keep working on it -- 
 this hut will be built much faster than other huts. By the way, any hut that has
 not been worked on yet can be relocated by dragging it
 around the map. Release it anywhere when its footprint is green
 .

Let's teach a villager to research...
 drag an adult villager to the large 
 table at the center of the big structure.

Great! This villager is learning to 
 research. As research skills improve, 
 you gain tech points that can be 
 spent like money on new technologies.

Let's check out the Technologies screen...
 click the 'Tech' button on the left side of 
 the screen.

Welcome to the Technologies screen.
 Use the tech points gained from research
 to upgrade a variety of different technologies.
 Click a '?' to learn more about a technology.

Children can also contribute to village life.
 Their keen eyes can spot mushrooms and small
 collectibles that adults might overlook.
 Drag a child to this collectible before it
 disappears.

Ooooh, the child found a collectible!
 Your villagers can collect Isola's small and
 beautiful treasures, but only when found by
 a child. The same collectible found more than
 once is converted into tech points.

Let's check out the Collections screen.
 Click the 'Collections' button on the left
 side of the screen.

Welcome to the Collections screen.
 Here you can see which collectibles your
 village children have gathered. Each set of collectibles
 benefits your tribe in some way. For example, each
 time you find a new piece of lab equipment, the
 researchers are permanently more productive!

Oh no! One of your little villagers is 
 sick. Let's train a healer. Find the sick 
 villager, then drag a second villager onto 
 the sick one.

Wonderful! The sick villager is better.
 Your healer also gained healing skill,
 which is essential for your villagers 
 to lead long and healthy lives.

Let's learn more about a villager...
 click the 'Detail' button at the 
 bottom of the screen.

Welcome to the Detail screen.
 Learn more about each villager, such 
 as age, health and skills. Check the 
 box to the right of a skill to set a 
 skill preference. Click 'Done' to return
 to the main screen.

Some of the mysteries of the island will require
 that other puzzles are solved first, or that 
 certain supplies have been made available. Let's
 help your villagers with an easy one-- making a
 supply of cutting tools. Drop someone on this giant
 fish skeleton on the beach.

Excellent! 
 Your villagers have 3 cutting tools available now. 
 They can make more any time they need them-- all you 
 have to do is drop another villager on the giant fish 
 skeleton again.

You can see the status of the game's puzzles on the Puzzles and Milestones screen. 
 Click the 'Puzzles' button on the left 
 side of the screen.

Welcome to the Puzzles and Milestones screen.
 The island is full of puzzles and hidden secrets
 waiting to be discovered. Your goal is to solve
 Isola's sixteen puzzles while helping your tribe
 survive.

Well, as we approach the conclusion of this tutorial, 
 we are really going to need that love shack finished. 
 Keep deploying villagers (especially ones with building 
 skill) on it until construction is complete.

Good!
 The love shack is a romantic hut and a perfect place 
 for village couples to discuss starting or adding to 
 their families and the tribe!

Let's make some babies...
 drag an adult male villager onto an 
 adult female villager or vice versa. 
 A villager will not seek a mate on 
 their own unless they are trained, and 
 Parenting is set as their preferred skill.

Good! They get along and want to
 go indoors for some privacy. With any 
 luck, the stork may bring a new baby.

Welcome to Virtual Villagers: The Tree Of Life
 
 Relief replaces panic as the villagers realize 
 that they have been granted success in their 
 quest for answers. They are certain that they 
 have been led to this forsaken, dying tree. As 
 they pray for continued guidance, they begin to 
 seek a way to save it . . . and all of Isola!

Almost! Click and hold the mouse button 
 anywhere on the ground and drag the 
 mouse to move around the village.

Good! Let's wait while the villager gathers blackberries. 
 If they succeed, they will bring some to
 the food bin near the center of the village.

Darn! The villager didn't succeed.
 Sometimes it takes a few tries, so drag
 the same villager to the blackberries again.

Good! Let's give the villager a 
 moment to research. If they 
 succeed, you will earn tech points.

Oh, well! The villager was unsuccessful 
 at research. Drag the same villager to 
 the table again.

Too bad! They didn't get along or 
 aren't in the mood. Try again with 
 the same couple or try a different 
 pair to see if love blossoms.

Congratulations! The stork brought 
 a baby. Be careful! A mother 
 cares for her child until age two and 
 won't do much else.

Shoot! The villager is still sick.
 Drag the same villager onto 
 the sick one again.

I'm sorry. One of your little villagers is dead.
 Villagers die of old age, but they can also die 
 from disease and starvation. Buying medicine 
 technology helps your villagers live longer 
 and have fewer diseases.

Welcome to the Overview Map. 
 Enjoy a bird's-eye view of your village,
 then click anywhere on the map to zoom
 in to that spot.

Virtual Villagers is a true real-time game.
 Your tribe continues to do what they have learned,
 even when the computer is off or you stop playing,
 but remember to check back often to care for 
 your little villagers! Have fun!

You have mastered the basics!
 How you manage your tribe now is up to you!
 Decide wisely who will do what. Your villagers 
 will slowly learn to do the tasks you show them.
 Once survival is no longer an issue, you can
 help them uncover the hidden secrets of Isola!
 Remember that the game continues to run, even
 when it is off, so keep a close eye on your tribe!

Hmmm... this villager is confused.
 Sometimes villagers need more skill 
 or more advanced technology before 
 they understand what to do.

Great! You set a villager's skill preference.
 From now on, they prefer this type of work 
 and gain skill the more they practice.

Nice try, but children don't work. They
 love to play and won't do what you ask 
 until they grow up. They can still help
 out though, as they sometimes find
 delicious mushrooms or collectibles.
Nursing mothers don't work while they \n are caring for an infant. \n
Good. Let's watch this villager make a supply \n of cutting tools for the tribe. \n

Congratulations! One of your villager's 
 reached the `Trainee` level in a skill 
 category.

Congratulations! One of your villager's 
 reached the `Adept` level in a skill 
 category.

Good job! Your villagers aren't worried about
 food anymore. Now you can focus on research
 and increasing the population of the village.

One of the young children of your tribe is now
 old enough to work! Your tribe needs every
 able-bodied person to help out, so find that
 villager and keep everyone productive.

One of your villagers is a master in a skill!
 This is a great accomplishment. Making any one
 villager a master in all five skills grants
 that villager the prestigious title of Scholar.
Congratulations! Your village reached\n its maximum sustainable population!\n
Your villagers found an interesting new\n recipe!\n

Alas, the fates were not kind to your village.
 All of your little villagers died. The island 
 of Isola remains a myth and its mysteries

The Clothing Hut

Fire!
 
 When a fire is burning, your villagers

Purify Tree!\n \n The tree has been purified.

Decorate Tree!
 
 The tree has been adorned with
 ceremonial ornaments.

Fish Scale Collection
 
 Your children collected all of the
 different fish scales found on Isola!
 Your maximum village population 
 is increased by 5.

Lab Equipment Collection
 
 Your children collected all of the
 different types of lab equipment found on 
 Isola! Your maximum village population 
 is increased by 5.

Mausoleum Mural Collection
 
 Your children collected all of the
 different mausoleum mural pieces found on 
 Isola! Your maximum village population 
 is increased by 5.

Wind Flute Collection
 
 Your children collected all of the
 different types of wind flutes found on 
 Isola! Your maximum village population 
 is increased by 5.

All Collections Complete!
 
 Well done! Your children completed all

One morning, the villagers noticed that the beach looked very wrong. The waves had ceased their normal rhythm, and the water had receded so far that it almost looked as though the ocean itself was drying up. Their apprehension became alarm as a powerful tsunami crashed down upon the village, obliterating structures, and, sadly, sweeping many villagers to a watery end.

One morning, the villagers noticed that there was an aggressive and toxic mold spreading inside the food bin and ruining the contents. The frantic villagers do their best to save the food, but they can't save it all...
It's springtime, and all the flowers are in bloom. Many of the villagers suffer a temporary bout of hay fever.
Today is the day that the villagers commemorate their arrival on the island of Isola with dancing, celebration, and feasts!
Today is the first day of the rainy season, marked by the first afternoon monsoon. Wow! It's really coming down!
An unseasonably cold, wet wind has blown through the village. The villagers were going to huddle around the fire, but the wet, icy drizzle put out the fire!

A freak wind has come up, filling the air with salt laden sand, apparently from some nearby salt flat. The salty dust is stifling and burning the villagers' eyes, and they all have to hide until things settle down.

The village is being pounded by a sudden, heavy rain, with drops the size of grapes! The villagers can barely see where they are going. This is certainly going to make it hard for them to get their chores done today.

Wasps have made their way through the brambles and started to make nests around the village. Unaware of the unwelcome visitors, the villagers continue playing and working nearby. Many villagers have been stung, and some of them are experiencing a bad reaction to the stings.

Today the villagers decide to celebrate collecting their 500th mushroom. Such industry from those little youngsters is indeed worthy of praise and glad celebration! There will be dancing and cake for the children.
The weather has been very pleasant lately, and the air smells especially pure and clean. Everyone's lungs feel great, and their stuffy noses have cleared right up!
The Canoe from the Other Side
A canoe has just landed on the beach, piloted by a villager from another part of Isola.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that a wealth of honeycombs have appeared, seemingly out of nowhere.\n \n Your village gains {award} food.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that someone or something has stolen some food.\n \n Your village has lost {award} food.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover a number of very useful scientific instruments that seem to have come out of nowhere, as though they simply fell from the sky.\n \n Your village has gained {award} tech points.

One morning the villagers notice that strange footprints have appeared on the ground overnight. They later discover that someone or something has stolen some important research tools.\n \n Your village has lost {award} tech points.
Today is the day that the villagers pay their respects to those who have passed on.

Today is the day that the villagers give thanks to those that guide their fate and for all the blessings they enjoy on the island of Isola. There will be dancing and ceremonies, followed by a sumptuous feast!

One of the more meticulous farmers has just noticed that there are a whole bunch of berries growing way in the back, where they had been previously overlooked. It looks like there are quite a few more berries left than they thought!

The villagers hear a racket in the distance that sounds like a large drum rolling down a hill. A moment later, they see a barrel with little heads peeking out of it appear at the top of the highest waterfall. Horrified, they watch it plummet down the waterfalls, until it reaches the pond. It bobs about in the water, and they manage to grab it before it sinks. Much to their relief, they find several giggling kids in the barrel, completely unharmed!
The villagers have been feeling glum and moody recently. Seeing the sacred tree in such a sorry state has had an adverse effect on their health and sense of well-being.
The villagers have been very happy and ambitious lately. Encouraged and inspired by the improving health of the sacred tree, everyone seems to feel rejuvenated.

As the sun comes up, the tribe is greeted by desperate crying coming from the bushes. Several babies have been abandoned by someone, although they have been carefully swaddled to keep them warm and comfortable. Some of the tribe's women graciously volunteer to take care of the poor infants.

After a rain, {name} sees an arc of brilliant colors in the sky. {He/She} has seen these before and knows that they don't last long, but {he/she} would like to know what is at the end of one. \n \n The left side of the arc appears to be near the mausoleum, while the right side appears to be dangerously close to the eastern cliff.

The arc grows fainter and fainter as {name} approaches its left side. Upon arriving at the mausoleum, {he/she} sees that there is no more trace of it. Perhaps it was sent from those who have passed on, so that they wouldn't be forgotten.

The arc seems to go just behind the cliff. Just a little further, and {he/she} can see what is back there. Oops! {name} falls from the cliff into the shallow water and hurts {his/her} head! {He/She} vows never to try anything like that again.

The arc seems to go just behind the cliff. Just a little further and {he/she} can see what is back there. Wow! {He/She} sees a huge patch of rare mushrooms and scoops them up for the tribe. \n \n Your tribe gains 300 food.
While looking for shells on the beach, {name} spots a rare robber crab. The tails of these crabs are known to have potent healing properties.

{name} brings the crab to the lab where they carefully remove its tail. The poor crab dies, but the healing fluid is easily extracted from the tail. Now that they know how to do this, the entire tribe becomes better healers.

Feeling sorry for the poor crab, {name} leaves it alone. Following the crab, {he/she} discovers that the crab has returned to a nest, where it has been storing food and covering it in salt crystals. When {he/she} explains this to the scientists, they develop a much better method for storing food. \n \n Your tribe gains a level of food mastery.
While searching for mushrooms, {name} sees a large, colorful fungus with bright dots on it. These bright mushrooms are known to be dangerous, and {he/she} wonders what to do with it.

{name} reaches down to pick the mushroom and cast it into the ocean. Upon touching it, {he/she} is gripped by vivid dreams and wakes up two days later with a splitting headache, but an unexplainable understanding of science.

{name} decides to leave the hazardous mushroom alone. Unfortunately, it multiplies over the next few weeks and somehow finds its way into their food source. Several from the tribe get sick, and others are acting strangely for days to come.

{name} has been having very bad abdominal pains all morning. By afternoon, {he/she} is overcome by pain and high fever. The villagers have been able to partially translate an ancient scroll, left by Isola's original inhabitants, that describes this illness exactly. The medical procedure is extremely dangerous and is barely within the villagers' technical reach.
Let the illness take its course

The villagers give {name} some special leaves and bark to chew for a while to help control pain. The procedure takes longer than expected, but, to the great relief of all concerned, {name} eventually makes a complete recovery. {name}, as a sign of gratitude towards the villagers, is inspired to study the medical arts and improve the medical knowledge of the tribe.

The villagers give {name} some special leaves and bark to chew for a while to help control pain. Shortly after the start of the procedure, grave complications arise and {name} worsens until {he/she} quietly passes away. The villagers grieve very much for {name} and reflect on their attempt to meddle with the natural order of things.

The villagers feel that the procedure is still out of their reach. Thanks to their years of research, though, they know that recovery can occur through the use of a regimen of herbal preparations. {name} survives, even though {his/her} health never fully returns. {name} has chronic stomach pains and finds it difficult to walk very far or stand up for long periods of time.
Late one night, {name} spots a mysterious figure working in the lab...

"Hello. My name is Biggles. Nice to meet you! Alas, I'm afraid you've seen too much." Biggles smiles, and raises a jeweled talisman. There is a flash of light. When {name} wakes up, {he/she} can't seem to remember anything, even {his/her} own name! Oddly, {name} seems to have somehow gained uncanny insights into matters of science.

Using ordinary equipment from the lab, the man performs a number of miraculous procedures far beyond the villager's knowledge. He knows he's being watched, and, without turning around, he says, "My name is Biggles. I am here to correct certain errors. You'll thank me later!" He puts some glowing objects in his pockets and vanishes in a blinding light. He has left behind some of his amazing improvised devices. \n \n Your village gains {award} tech points.
{name} sees a gorgeous pink shell on the beach. {He/She} wonders what to do with it.
Pick it up and listen inside

{name} picks up the beautiful shell and holds it up to {his/her} ear, because {he/she} has been told that you can hear the ocean in such things. Ow!! A tiny crab is living in the shell and bites {name} on the ear before scuttling away. Well, needless to say, {name} is not a fan of crabs anymore.
It's such a pretty shell! What's this? The shell appears to grow legs and scuttles away. {name} develops a new appreciation for life on the island.
{name} found a hollow bamboo tube embedded neatly in the ground. Inside, it has some notches. {He/She} wonders what to do with it and considers pouring some water into it.
Fill it up to the first notch

After filling it to the first notch, {name} puzzles over how the device might work. Consulting with the scientists, {he/she} determines that this device can be used to predict the tides. \n \n The tribe gains 3000 tech points and learns that the tide pool is accessible every 2 hours.

{name} fills it to the top and speculates about the use of this device. {He/She} consults the scientists, and they determine that it should be filled only to the first notch. A heated argument ensues, because there is no way to remove the water right now. The scuffle in the lab has damaged some experiments, and the tribe is left with only dubious assumptions about this device.\n \n The tribe loses 2000 tech points

{name} decides to climb the great banyan, thinking that it would be a great achievement to climb the Tree of Life! Unfortunately {he/she} gets stuck at the top of the tree and can't figure out how to get back down.
Try to find a way down

The first step was a bad one. {name} tumbles down through the branches, badly hurting {his/her} leg, and lands behind the tree. {He/She} lies there for a full day and night before being discovered and rescued by the tribe. This time let {him/her} bond with the tree in an unexpected way.\n \n Your tribe gains a level of Dendrology tech.

{name} calls for help, and members of the tribe quickly come to the rescue and tell {him/her} to try to climb down. {He/She} takes a tentative first step and falls, but is caught by the waiting tribe members. Embarrassment and lost productivity are all there is to show for this misadventure.\n \n Your tribe loses 500 tech points.
{name} notices that there are mosquito larvae collecting in the pond. Nobody wants a mosquito infestation, so the villagers decide that they should try to do something about them.
After putting soap in the pond, the tribe discovers that the only effect of adding the soap is that they are being eaten alive by very clean mosquitoes.

Using oil from various plants, the tribe covers the pond water with a thin layer of oil. The mosquito larvae, unable to breathe, quickly perish.\n \n The tribal scientists observe this and gain 500 tech points.

{name} is relieved that the tribe, while skeptical, decides that it's wise to investigate these glowing faces. They discover that they are actually luminous algae in the bushes. The scientists eagerly harvest them for use in the lab.\n \n Your tribe gains 1000 tech points.
{name} tries to pretend they don't exist. {He/She} doesn't sleep well anymore, and becomes jumpy and restless and much less effective at work.

{name} is having a difficult time with her baby, who won't stop screaming. She is receiving conflicting advice from the other villagers. Some say the baby should be left alone in a dark, quiet place to calm itself. Others suggest that the baby needs a fun diversion and advise her to take the baby to the beach and dance around.
The baby's screaming gets more and more desperate until everyone in the tribe is distracted. Eventually it cries itself to sleep, and mommy is a mess.
The soothing sound of the ocean, combined with the rhythmic dancing, lull the baby into a blissful sleep. Mommy got a much-needed rest and is very grateful to the tribe for their help.

{name} is swimming in the ocean one day when {he/she} bumps into a floating box. It appears to be carefully sealed, and {he/she} wants to bring it back to the village, but the tide is pulling it out. It would be very risky to try and swim back with this box.

{name} barely manages to get the box back to the beach. Upon opening it, the tribe finds glass bottles of all sizes. These will certainly change how they work in the lab. \n \n Your tribe gains 5000 tech points.

Making slow progress, {name} proceeds to drag the box to the beach. Larger and larger waves crash against {him/her}, but the shore is getting closer. Suddenly an enormous wave blocks out the sun and turns the water white. When the ocean calms again, the box is floating back out to sea, and {name} is nowhere to be seen.

{name} seriously doubts that {he/she} can safely bring the box back. Whatever was inside could not make up for the loss of {his/her} life. {He/She} gives it a shove, and the box floats farther and farther out to sea until it is out of sight.

{name} is strolling along the beach one morning when {he/she} trips over something covered in algae. {He/She} removes the algae and finds a waterlogged book. Opening the cover, which disintegrates almost immediately, {name} sees that it appears to be a book of knowledge, but the pages are falling apart. {He/She} has two choices: read each page as it disintegrates or try to carefully carry the whole thing back to the lab.

{He/She} is barely able to read each page before the waterlogged parchment turns to mush. There is a section on farming, a section on building, a section on everything. {name} feels enriched by the text but regrets that {he/she} was unable to share it with the tribe.

Despite carefully cradling the book and rushing back to the lab, by the time {he/she} gets there, only one section of the book is still intact. The remaining section contains practices and techniques for nurturing children. The entire tribe studies the text and is grateful for what they were able to salvage.

{name} found a delicious rare mushroom and ate it, instead of bringing it back to the food bin as {he/she} had been taught to do. An adult was nearby and asked, "What are you doing, little one?" {He/She} isn't sure what to say.

{name} denies eating the mushroom. The adult silently looks at {him/her} for a long time, and then walks off. Immediately afterward {name} feels ashamed and remorseful. {He/She} decides to make up for it on {his/her} own by skipping meals for a week.

{name} admits to eating the mushroom. The adult says, "You know that was wrong. Now go help the farmers pick blackberries -- and no dinner for you tonight." {name} feels better at having told the truth and learns a lot by helping the farmers that afternoon. They also let {him/her} nibble on blackberries.
{name} has fallen gravely ill. {He/She} is also an aspiring healer and has long theorized that pure algae from the sea has healing properties.
The algae is nutritious, if not delicious. Whether it was due to healing properties or just additional nourishment from the algae is hard to say, but {name} feels better and has learned something.
{name} decides to stick to the tried and true and not risk experimenting with unproven remedies. The disease will have to run its course.
{name} has fallen gravely ill. {He/She} is also an aspiring healer and has long theorized that water from the magnificent ocean surrounding Isola should have healing properties.
{name} bravely drinks {his/her} fill of ocean water from a wooden bowl. A few moments later {he/she} becomes violently ill and is worse off than before.

{name} thinks that it's better to listen to one's body, and {his/her} body is definitely telling {him/her} not to drink ocean water. {He/She} decides to apply this philosophy in the study of medicine. Although {name} is still sick, {he/she} feels a bit wiser.
{name} has fallen gravely ill. {He/She} is also an aspiring healer and has long theorized that the bright, forbidden mushrooms that grow under rocks have healing properties, if eaten in TINY amounts.

{name} takes a tiny nibble of the bright, forbidden mushroom. It tastes bitter and dry. A couple of hours later {he/she} has violent fits, but the next morning the illness seems to have passed. That wasn't exactly a pleasant way to get through the sickness, but it did work, and {he/she} learned something.
It's better to not mess with dangerous mushrooms. After all, it is probably just a bad cold. {name} decides to just wait the illness out.
{name} has fallen gravely ill. {He/She} is also an aspiring healer and has long theorized that eating a bit of bark from the Tree of Life would have to be healthful.

{name} takes a bit of shaved bark from the tree and nibbles on it. The bitter juices actually have a pleasant flavor. It could just be coincidence, but the next morning {he/she} feels considerably better.
It's better to not mess with eating random things. {name} decides to just wait the illness out.
{name} has fallen gravely ill. {He/She} is also an aspiring healer and has long wondered if fasting for a full day would cleanse the body of the poisons causing the illness.
{name} foregoes all food for a full 24 hours. The next day {he/she} is still sick, feels even worse, and is very weak from hunger. Oh well, at least it is a lesson learned.
{name} is just too hungry to pull this off. Maybe next time.

{name} has suffered a painful cut on {his/her} leg. {He/She} is an aspiring healer and has long wondered which would be a more effective way to treat such a wound: mashed bark from the Tree of Life or mashed up rare mushrooms.

{name} makes a mushy paste with smashed tree bark from the Tree of Life. {He/She} packs the mush into the cut and notices immediately that the pain lessens. By the next morning the wound is almost healed! {name} gains useful medicine knowledge from the experiment!

{name} figures that mushrooms are good for people, so maybe they would help in an open cut. {He/She} mashes up mushrooms and softens them with sea water. Then {he/she} spreads this paste into the cut. The next morning, the cut is festering and yellow. Oh well, live and learn!

{name} is a very curious individual. {He/She} is eager to conduct innovative experiments in the lab, but wasteful and dangerous experiments are discouraged by the others. In the dark of night, {he/she} is trying a new one: A mixture of the smelly yellow salts of the pond, coal from the fire, and one other ingredient. Should {he/she} try the white salts from the rocky cliff or dried algae?

{name} finishes the concoction using the white salts. {He/She} was hoping for a healing salve, but it seems too coarse to use. Maybe heating it up over a fire...BOOM! The mixture promptly explodes with unusual force. {name} is injured, but the scientists learn an interesting new chemical composition. \n \n The tribe gains 2000 tech points.

Putting the algae into the mixture just made a dusty, crunchy mess that smelled mildly foul. {name} tried adding water to mix the ingredients better, but it just made a disgusting greenish-brown sludge that ended up being a waste of research materials. \n \n The tribe loses 1000 tech points.

{name} has devised a new way to approach hut construction. {He/She} believes that having a worker at the top of the structure to hoist building materials to the top would make hut construction more efficient. {He/She} volunteers to test the technique, despite it being extremely dangerous. A fall could mean injury or even death!

{name} climbs up high on a scaffolding and demonstrates {his/her} new technique to the tribe. The new method of lifting wood and supplies to the hard-to-reach areas of the structure is a great success. {He/She} is certainly becoming a skilled builder!
Perched at the top of a scaffolding, {name} tries to stay on {his/her} feet but soon loses {his/her} balance and falls a great distance to the hard ground.

It could work, but {name} does not think it is worth the risk. Any advantage gained by innovative work techniques would never make up for all the pain and trouble of a serious injury. Better just forget it.

{name} believes that the fruit would cook faster in the cooking pit if {he/she} was balanced on top of the covered fruit, applying constant pressure while it cooks. This is obviously extremely dangerous, but could it work?

{name} sets the fruit under a banana leaf and begins to balance on the hard round bump. In a few moments the fruit begins to soften, and {name} quickly hops off and retrieves the cooked fruit! It is very effective and {name} is setting the bar among farmers!

{name} sets the fruit under a banana leaf and prepares to step onto the fruit. Even before {his/her} foot reaches the covered fruit, {he/she} slips and stumbles into the hot coals! That was a bad idea...
{name} knows better than to try this kind of crazy thing. Those coals are hot, and very unforgiving.

{name} hears crying and finds a village child stuck high up on a branch in the great Tree of Life. No amount of coaxing will bring {him/her} down. It will be very dangerous for an adult to climb that high on the tree and help the child down. Perhaps the child should be left to have a lesson about consequences.

{name} climbs up the tree and helps the child find a path back down through the branches. Predictably, {name}'s own descent does not go so smoothly. The second branch {he/she} touches snaps loudly! {name} tumbles down through the branches and hits the ground hard. Oh well, parenting requires sacrifices.

Children have to learn about the consequences of their actions. {name} leaves the child. Hours later the small, subdued youth returns to the village, bruised and angry. It is not obvious whether it was a lesson about consequences or just a lesson about falling down.

Two children have been constantly fighting over a pretty, round shell.{name} is sick of the bickering and decides to intervene. The children will have to either be taught to share the shell, or they will have to decide who will keep it.
Sharing is important, and teaching children about this is good parenting. They agree to share the shell, and {name} reflects on how well this went.

Not everything can be shared, and in this case a lesson about negotiation is more valuable. However, even after they pick an owner for the shell, one of the children feels very bad, outmatched at the debate over the shell. Still, the fighting has stopped. {name}'s approach was innovative and effective, although maybe a bit harsh.

{name} discovers a mysterious figure lurking by the tree one night. Sensing {name}, the figure turns, smiles and says: "Hello, my child. My name is Biggles. Perhaps you have heard of me? I have been watching you. Your people have done well in returning the balance to Isola. I will tell you something: The island, like life, is a wheel. This tree you see here is its axle. To restore balance the axle must be true. Now, because your people are worthy, I will answer one question:"
How should we care for our people?
How should we care for the tree?

"Yes, I see that you are a good and caring people. I will teach you a secret." Biggles teaches {name} some advanced and arcane medical knowledge. When {name} turns to thank him, he is simply not there! Where could he have gone?

"Yes, I see that you are a good and wise people. I will teach you a secret." Biggles teaches {name} some advanced and arcane techniques in dendrology. When {name} turns to thank him, he is simply not there! Where could he have gone?
